question: Two careful engineers implementing this rule independently, with only this contract, would produce DIFFERENT behavior on some input (the rule is ambiguous, under-specified, or relies on unstated host facts).

rules.text: Each text is split into lines on U+000A (LINE FEED) only. Every other character, U+000D, U+2028, U+2029 and U+FEFF included, is ordinary line content. A text with k line feeds has k + 1 lines; the empty text is one empty line, and a text ending in a line feed ends with an empty line.

Lines are visited at the same index from index 0 up to the larger line count; the FIRST index where the two sides disagree decides, with i its 0-based index. They disagree when one side has no line at i (R3) or both have one and the two lines are different sequences of code points (R4).

MISSING LINE. When existing has no line i -> "line " + decimal(i + 1) + ": existing has no line " + decimal(i + 1) + ", profile has " + WINDOW(the profile line, 0). Symmetrically, when profile has no line i -> "line " + decimal(i + 1) + ": profile has no line " + decimal(i + 1) + ", existing has " + WINDOW(the existing line, 0). Since each side has at least one line, i >= 1 here. A trailing line feed on one side only is reported this way (the present line is empty).

DIFFERING LINES. c = the length of the longest common prefix of the two lines in code points (0-based; c never exceeds the shorter line's length). Result -> "line " + decimal(i + 1) + ", col " + decimal(c + 1) + ": existing " + WINDOW(the existing line, c) + " vs profile " + WINDOW(the profile line, c).
EQUAL. When no index disagrees (the texts are identical) -> the text "binary difference (the texts decode to the same UTF-8)". CITED FIDELITY package

WINDOW(s, c) for a line s of L code points = QUOTE, then ELLIPSIS when c > 0, then ESCAPE of each code point of s at positions c up to but excluding min(c + WIDTH, L), in order, then ELLIPSIS when c + WIDTH < L, then QUOTE. When c = L the middle is empty: the shorter side of a prefix pair renders as QUOTE ELLIPSIS QUOTE when c > 0. The two ELLIPSIS marks are added, never escaped; WIDTH counts source code points, not the escaped length.

ESCAPE maps one code point to text by the first row of TABLE ESCAPE that applies. Escapes are per code point and context-free; hex digits are lowercase; the four-digit and braced forms are chosen by the row. The window is a supplementary character's whole encoding or none of it (positions are code points), but a cut may fall inside a grapheme: between regional indicators, before a combining mark, a variation selector or a zero width joiner. CITED FIDELITY package
U+0022 QUOTATION MARK                      -> backslash, then U+0022
any other code point U+0000 through U+001F -> backslash, "u", four lowercase hex digits of the code point
a code point in INVISIBLE at or below U+FFFF -> backslash, "u", four lowercase hex digits of the code point
a code point in INVISIBLE above U+FFFF     -> backslash, "u", "{", the lowercase hex digits of the code point with no
anything else                              -> the code point itself, unchanged
